_about: In His Steps: the Christian edition, for daily quiet times. Same app as A Life Well Lived,
with its own name, welcome page, quotes, colors and voices. The library of quotable
works is sources.json in this folder (made by tools/make_christian_sources.py), and
Claude's instructions are in prompts/. Run it with EDITION=christian.

tab_drawing.about: The browser-tab icon: the sandal from the welcome page (keep these paths in step with the 'sandal' icon in templates/index.html).

description: A private journal for your daily quiet time, with a reflection from Scripture after every entry.
lead: A quiet place for reflection, drawing on deep Christian wisdom.

points.title: A few lines are enough
points.text: The benefit of journaling comes from reflecting each day. A prompt is there when the page feels blank.

points.title: A well-stocked library of Christian wisdom
points.text: Reflections draw only on selected books of Scripture and classic devotional writers such as Augustine, Brother Lawrence, Bunyan, Wesley, Spurgeon and Andrew Murray, and tell you exactly where to find each passage.

points.title: Grow in His Steps
points.text: Every reflection ends with an honest question to carry through your day. Easily find favorite entries and passages.

points.title: Private, and never used to train AI
points.text: Entries are encrypted with a passphrase only you know. Your entry is only used to write your daily reflection, and isn’t used to train AI.

welcome_quote.text: “Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns.”

promises: Every verse checked, word for word, with a link to read it in context.
A companion for quiet contemplation, pointing you to Scripture, to prayer, and to the words of Jesus.
Made to deepen your prayer and your quiet time, never to stand in for them or for your pastor.

check_example.intro: For example, if a reflection quotes Ecclesiastes 11:4 in the wording of another translation (the ESV):
check_example.quoted: He who observes the wind will not sow, and he who regards the clouds will not reap.
check_example.shown_intro: the app finds the verse and shows it as the Berean Standard Bible has it:
check_example.shown: He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.

foundation: In His Steps is rooted in the Protestant devotional tradition: Scripture is the final authority, and salvation is by grace through faith. Its reflections are written for believers from many churches, and steer clear of the questions that divide them.

reflection_rules.title: How reflections are written
items: As a fellow traveler. A reflection never speaks for God or tells you what He thinks of you. It brings the words of people who walked the same road: the Psalmists, Paul, Peter, and the writers who came after them.
The words of Jesus, as He said them. His sayings are quoted word for word from the Gospels, and never stretched into what He would say about your situation.
Toward prayer and your church. Reflections encourage prayer, trust in God, and the people around you. They're no substitute for Scripture, a pastor, or a friend who knows you.
Checked before you see it. Every quotation is matched against its source, as described above.
With care in hard times. If an entry suggests real distress, the reflection sets everything else aside, responds with care, and shows where to find help.

selection.title: Why these books and writers
selection.text: The books of the Bible here are chosen for a daily quiet time: the Psalms and the wisdom books, the stories of Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Ruth and David, the prophets of comfort and lament, the Gospels and Acts, and the letters. Each comes with notes that steer reflections to the passages meant for devotion, and away from genealogies, laws and judgments that need more context than a short reflection can give. The writers are among the most widely loved devotional voices of the Protestant tradition, from the early church to the twentieth century. A few stronger or more contested voices start switched off.

translation_note.title: Why the Berean Standard Bible?
translation_note.text: Two reasons. It reads easily: the BSB is a modern translation from the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek, in plain, natural English that stays close to the original wording. And it is free to quote: its publishers dedicated it to the public domain in 2023, so this journal can quote any verse, check every quotation against the complete text, and link you to the passage, without the permissions and limits that copyrighted translations such as the NIV or ESV carry. If you read another translation, the wording here may differ a little from what you know.

recurring_scripture.about: Every couple of reflections, a nudge toward the words of Jesus (journal/reflection.py)
recurring_scripture.note: Neither of this person's last two reflections quoted the words of Jesus. If a saying of Jesus in the Gospels genuinely meets this entry, quote it this time, word for word, introduced as His words. If none truly fits, don't force one.

examples.paraphrase: Paul told the Philippians not to be anxious about anything, but to bring every request to God with thanksgiving.
examples.reference: Brother Lawrence, in his Fourth Conversation, described…
examples.quote_intro: As Paul wrote to the Romans, [[q1]]

writers.name: Augustine
writers.guide: the restless heart that finds rest only in God; disordered loves, loving good things in the wrong order; the divided will; confession as both admitting sin and praising God.

writers.name: Thomas Aquinas
writers.guide: grace that perfects nature; faith, hope and charity as gifts that grow; pride as the root of sin and humility as the ground of the other virtues; sloth as sorrow over spiritual good.

writers.name: Thomas à Kempis
writers.guide: following Christ in humility; knowing yourself; inner peace through a quiet conscience; bearing with others' faults as you hope they bear with yours.

writers.name: Martin Luther
writers.guide: justified by faith alone, free from the need to earn God's favor; the Christian as free lord of all and dutiful servant of all; good works flowing from a freed heart, for the neighbor's sake; honest wrestling with doubt and temptation.

writers.name: John Calvin
writers.guide: we are not our own, but God's; self-denial as the sum of the Christian life; bearing the cross; using this world's gifts gratefully without being owned by them; knowing God and knowing ourselves.

writers.name: Richard Baxter
writers.guide: heavenly-mindedness as medicine for an earth-bound heart; looking ahead to the rest that remains, and letting it steady the present.

writers.name: John Owen
writers.guide: mortifying sin by the Spirit, at its root, by looking to Christ ("be killing sin or it will be killing you").

writers.name: Richard Sibbes
writers.guide: Christ's gentleness with the weak: the bruised reed He will not break, the smoking flax He will not quench; a little grace is still grace, and worth more than it feels.

writers.name: Jeremiah Burroughs
writers.works: The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
writers.guide: contentment as something learned, not handed over; reached by wanting less rather than having more; a quiet heart under a hard providence.

writers.name: John Bunyan
writers.guide: the Christian life as a pilgrimage, with a burden lifted at the cross, the Slough of Despond, Vanity Fair, Doubting Castle and Giant Despair, the key called Promise; his own story of a troubled conscience finding grace.

writers.name: Brother Lawrence
writers.guide: practicing the presence of God in ordinary work; turning back to God simply, without self-reproach, after distraction.

writers.name: Jonathan Edwards
writers.guide: true religion lying largely in holy affections; strong feelings proving nothing either way; the surest sign of grace being a changed life.

writers.name: John Wesley
writers.guide: grace that goes before us, forgives and changes; holiness of heart and life; love made complete; faith working by love; the plain use of time, money and the means of grace.

writers.name: John Newton
writers.guide: grace toward a great sinner, and patience with slow growth; plain pastoral counsel on lingering sin, assurance, and bearing with other people's faults as God bears with ours.

writers.name: Charles Spurgeon
writers.guide: warm, vivid daily meditation on a single verse; Christ's sufficiency for the weak and the weary.

writers.name: J. C. Ryle
writers.guide: holiness as the fruit of grace and the mark of real faith; the daily fight; counting the cost; Christ is all.

writers.name: Andrew Murray
writers.guide: abiding in Christ; humility as the creature's true place and the root of every grace, tested most among other people; prayer learned at Jesus' feet.

writers.name: Hannah Whitall Smith
writers.guide: trust as rest: handing a burden over and leaving it there; faith as a choice of the will rather than a feeling; what to do after failure.

writers.name: George MacDonald
writers.guide: God as a Father whose love is a consuming fire that will have us wholly good; childlikeness; obedience as the door to knowing God; honest doubt brought to God rather than hidden.
writers.caution: He hoped all would at last be saved and rejected some common accounts of the atonement: draw on his picture of the Father's love and of obedience, not on those arguments.

writers.name: E. M. Bounds
writers.guide: prayer as the real work rather than the preparation for it; much time alone with God; beginning the day with prayer; the heart before the head.

writers.name: Oswald Chambers
writers.guide: utter surrender to God; obedience in the ordinary day rather than in great moments.

writers.name: A. W. Tozer
writers.guide: hungering for God Himself rather than religious activity; the sacrament of ordinary living.

writers.name: G. K. Chesterton
writers.guide: wonder and gratitude at the sheer gift of existing; humility that doubts itself rather than the truth; joy as the secret of the Christian; loving the world enough to want it changed.

writers.name: C. S. Lewis
writers.guide: pride as the great sin; the longing for joy that nothing in this world satisfies.
writers.works: Mere Christianity, The Screwtape Letters, The Weight of Glory

writers.name: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
writers.guide: costly grace against cheap grace; life together, and bearing with one another in it.
writers.works: The Cost of Discipleship, Life Together

writers.name: Leonard Ravenhill
writers.guide: prayer as the true measure of a life; eternity kept in view; holiness that costs something.
writers.caution: Draw on his seriousness about prayer and eternity, never a scolding tone.
writers.works: Why Revival Tarries, Revival Praying, Meat for Men

writers.name: Derek Prince
writers.guide: faith that comes by hearing God's word and is lived by decision; prayer joined with fasting; yielding your rights and trusting God with the outcome.
writers.caution: Draw only on these themes. Never bring in his teaching on demons, deliverance or curses.
writers.works: Shaping History Through Prayer and Fasting, Faith to Live By, The Grace of Yielding, Foundational Truths for the Christian Life

writers.name: Corrie ten Boom
writers.works: The Hiding Place, Tramp for the Lord
writers.guide: forgiving what seems unforgivable, as an act of the will helped by God; no pit so deep that God's love is not deeper; thankfulness in hard places; worry as carrying tomorrow's load today.

writers.name: Elisabeth Elliot
writers.works: Through Gates of Splendor, Keep a Quiet Heart, A Path Through Suffering
writers.guide: obedience in the next ordinary duty; suffering received rather than explained away; loneliness and waiting offered to God; a quiet heart.

writers.name: John Stott
writers.works: Basic Christianity, The Cross of Christ
writers.guide: the cross at the center of everything; clear thinking joined to humble living; faith that engages the whole mind and the world around it.

writers.name: J. I. Packer
writers.guide: knowing God rather than knowing about Him; being God's adopted child as the heart of the gospel; God's wisdom in the things we cannot understand.

writers.name: Richard Foster
writers.guide: the spiritual disciplines (prayer, fasting, simplicity, solitude, service) as the way into freedom, not a new law; superficiality as the curse of our age.

writers.name: Eugene Peterson
writers.works: A Long Obedience in the Same Direction, Eat This Book
writers.guide: discipleship as a long obedience in the same direction; unhurried attention to God in an ordinary place among ordinary people; reading Scripture slowly, to be changed by it.

writers.name: Dallas Willard
writers.guide: spiritual disciplines as training rather than trying; the renovation of the heart.
writers.works: The Spirit of the Disciplines, Renovation of the Heart

writers.name: Tim Keller
writers.guide: idols of the heart, good things made ultimate; the gospel that humbles and lifts up at once.
writers.works: The Reason for God, Counterfeit Gods, The Prodigal God

sources_intro: Reflections quote only the works below. Every quotation is checked word for word against the text before you see it, and links to the passage it came from; if it can't be confirmed, the reflection puts the idea in its own words instead. Scripture is from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB), a modern translation from the Hebrew and Greek, dedicated to the public domain in 2023. The other writers are in public-domain editions from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library (CCEL), Project Gutenberg and Wikisource.

source_groups.name: The Law and the story of Israel
source_groups.about: Beginnings, the Exodus and the wilderness, and the lives of Ruth, Hannah, Samuel and David.

source_groups.name: Wisdom and poetry
source_groups.about: Job's honest suffering, the Psalms for prayer in every mood, and the wisdom of Proverbs and Ecclesiastes.

source_groups.name: The Prophets
source_groups.about: Isaiah's comfort, Jeremiah and Lamentations in grief and hope, and three short prophets: Jonah, Micah and Habakkuk.

source_groups.name: The Gospels and Acts
source_groups.about: The life and teaching of Jesus, including the Sermon on the Mount and the parables, and the first Christians.

source_groups.name: Paul's letters
source_groups.about: Grace, freedom and the new life in Christ, above all in Romans, Galatians, Ephesians and Philippians.

source_groups.name: Hebrews and the general letters
source_groups.about: Faith that endures and faith that works: Hebrews, James, Peter and John.

source_groups.name: The early and medieval church
source_groups.about: Augustine's restless heart and Aquinas on grace and the virtues.

source_groups.name: Devotional classics
source_groups.about: Two Catholic classics long treasured by Protestants: following Christ in humility, and practicing God's presence in ordinary work.

source_groups.name: The Reformation
source_groups.about: Freedom by faith alone, and the shape of the Christian life.

source_groups.name: The Puritans
source_groups.about: Searching the heart, fighting sin by the Spirit, and the pilgrim road.

source_groups.name: Revival and the evangelical tradition
source_groups.about: From the Great Awakening to the turn of the 20th century: true religion, holiness of heart and life, daily devotion, humility, trust and prayer.

source_groups.name: The twentieth century
source_groups.about: Wonder and gratitude in Chesterton, and Tozer's hunger for God Himself.

paraphrase_only.about: Reflections may draw on these writers' ideas in their own words, naming the writer and book, but never quote them, and there are no links. Most are still in copyright; for a few older writers the app doesn't yet have a text to check quotations against.
